I've been farming this land for over 30 years. My husband and I have about 7 mu between the two of us, all flat ground good for grain. In Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat and summer corn — it's what the soil is for, it's what the buyers want, and I know it cold. I wouldn't grow something I don't know.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after the soil cools. I'll buy improved seed from the village co-op — the same variety I used last year because it did well. I water at sowing, again at jointing, and at heading if it's dry. I put down base fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress urea at jointing. One or two pesticide sprays for aphids and powdery mildew in spring.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant corn immediately — no time to waste, the season is short. I use a hybrid, same one the neighbors use, Zhengdan 958 or similar. Corn needs less water than wheat but I'll irrigate if it doesn't rain around silking. Topdress urea at the big bell stage. Spray once for corn borer if I see the damage.

I use rotary tillage before wheat and leave the corn stubble cut short. Plowing is too expensive now with fuel prices.
